newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: PUBLISHER TO ASSIST RIGHT WING HISTORIAN
The publisher of British right-wing historian, David Irving, says she'd be surprised if he is turned away in his latest attempt to enter Australia.
Mr Irving was refused a visa in 1992, but says he'll lodge a new application following Prime Minister John Howard's comments on freedom of speech.
Mr Irving is also banned from Canada, Germany and Austria for questioning the Holocaust and associating with neo-nazi elements.
His publisher in Australia, Veritas Publishing, has funded his previous legal fights to gain a visa and Jan Pope, who runs the company, says she and her husband may support Mr Irving again.
DALAI LAMA'S HOPES FOR FUTURE
The Dalai Lama says he hopes the next century will be the century of dialogue, because this one will go down as the century of bloodshed.
The Tibetan spiritual leader was addressing an audience in Sydney last night about his hopes for the future.
He says basic human qualities such as compassion must be displayed for someone to be a good person, though he believes it's okay not to be religious.
Prime Minister John Howard will hold a meeting with the Dalai Lama tomorrow, against the wishes of the Chinese Government.
CHINA SLATES ONE CHINA POLICY
China's Communist Party has attacked the Australian Government's one China policy, describing it as absurd.
The criticism came in an article released by the State-run Xinhua news agency, after Prime Minister John Howard confirmed he will meet the exiled Tibetan spirtiual leader, the Dalai Lama.
The article says Australian politicians' willingness to meet the Dalai Lama is inconsistent with their expressed support for a one China policy.

The article accuses Australian politicians of having ulterior motives and of interfering in China's internal affairs. China annexed Tibet in the 1950s, claiming a sovereignty over the country it says dates back 700 years.
GREENS SAY TEST BAN TREATY A TOKEN
Greens Senator, Dee Margetts, says Australia has been weak in not pushing for a timetable for nuclear disarmament.
She says the comprehensive test ban treaty signed by the five nuclear powers at the United Nations, is a token, because it'll probably never come into force.
That's because India is refusing to sign the document.
Senator Margetts says Australia should have pushed for a timetable for disarmament when the World Court recently declared the threat or use of nuclear weapons illegal.
And she says Australia should be using the Canberra Commission, as a lever for a disarmament timetable.
AIRPORT MAINTENANCE CLOSURE CONDEMNED
Union and community leaders in Geelong have condemned the closure of the ASTAAS aircraft maintenance company, with the loss of more than 450 jobs.
The company's board yesterday announced the immediate closure of the plant at Avalon airport.
The Federal Government says a buyer for the firm couldn't be found because the heavy aircraft maintenance market is depressed.
But, Geelong Trades and Labor Council secretary, John Kranz, says the Government and the board have turned their back on Geelong and all of regional Australia.
He wants a meeting with the ASTAAS board this morning to find out how hard it tried to find a buyer.
Meanwhile, Geelong's Acting Mayor Adrienne Edgar says the closure means the loss of technology and expertise to a region with 8-and-a half per cent unemployment.
VIETNAM VETS DISAPPOINTED WITH GOVT
The Vietnam Veterans' Association is bitterly disappointed with the Federal Government's decision to do more research into a possible link between agent orange and spina bifida in veteran's children.
Veterans Affairs Minister, Bruce Scott, has called for research saying the evidence of a link is weak and could be due to chance.
But he says the Government would act if new evidence comes to light.
The Veterans' Association says that's not enough considering action in the United States.
The U.S. Government has already accepted responsibility, apologised and legislated for compensation.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
